title: Breathing harmful gases causes lung damage
author: timothymtorres
body:
## About The Pull Request
This adds lung damage whenever a mob is breathing bad atmospherics:
- Breathing extreme heat/cold gas (below `120K` or above `1000K`) deals a flat `3` lung damage per tick
- Breathing Plasma or Freon (Oxygen for Plasmamen) deals `0.5` lung damage per partial pressure
- Breathing Tritium and Antinoblium deals `1.0` lung damage per partial pressure
- Breathing Zauker deals `2.0` lung damage per partial pressure
- Lung damage is clamped between `0.1` (min) and `15` (max) per breath

Useful Context: 
- Breathing ticks occur every 8-second interval normally however:
  - it is 2 seconds faster if your lungs or heart are heavily damaged (stacking together, down to 4 seconds)
  - if you failed your last breath, then it's every 2-second interval
- Standard cigarettes deal `1.0` lung damage every 2 seconds
- Opening a full canister of pure gas in a medium-sized area results in about ~20pp of the gas type

Misc Changes:
- Add Antinoblium breath effects since it was missing (just a more radioactive and toxic version of Tritium)
- Nitrium lung damage is clamped using our new damage max/min formula 
- Plasmaman oxygen damage type has been switched from `OXYGEN` to `TOXIN`, matching the inverse relationship of humans inhaling Plasma

## Why It's Good For The Game
This integrates lung damage into passive environmental hazards. Organ damage mechanics are a robust part of medical gameplay, but in practice, they are rarely interacted with unless a player self-inflicts them. (heavy drinking for liver damage, smoking for lung damage, welding without goggles for eye damage, etc.) Atmospheric disasters like freon leaks, plasma fires, and extreme temperature shifts now have lasting medical consequences. Running through a burning or contaminated hallway without internals creates lingering lung trauma that requires proper medical treatment.

Because players typically put on internals or evacuate a hazard zone within 5–10 seconds, it is balanced so that brief exposure causes mild lung damage, while prolonged exposure leads to organ failure before regular mob damage (brute, o2, toxin, etc.) outright kills the player.

Organ Failure Timelines:
| Hazard Scenario | Damage Per Breath | Organ Failure ETA |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Tritium (10pp) & Plasma (20pp) Fire | 20 | 5 breathes (10 - 20 seconds) |
| Standard Plasma Fire (20pp) | 10 | 10 breathes (20 - 40 seconds) |
| Heavy Toxic Gas (Freon 10pp) | 5 | 20 breathes (40 seconds - 1 min) |
| Hull Breach Space (Cold Air) | 3 | 30 breathes (1 min - 2 min) |
| Trace Toxic Gas (Plasma 2pp) | 1 | 100 breathes (3 min - 5 min) |

changes.text: Add toxic and radioactive effects to breathing Antinoblium.
Breathing harmful gases causes lung damage. (scales with partial pressure)
Plasmamen breathing oxygen now causes TOXIN damage.

title: makes sure smoothing stays paused through atom initialization fixing a race condition
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

```
runtime error: bad index
proc name: bitmask smooth (/atom/proc/bitmask_smooth)
source file: code/__HELPERS/icon_smoothing.dm,251
src: the full tile window (/obj/structure/window/fulltile)
call stack:
the full tile window (/obj/structure/window/fulltile): bitmask smooth()
the full tile window (/obj/structure/window/fulltile): smooth icon()
Icon Smoothing (/datum/controller/subsystem/icon_smooth): fire()
```

Icon smoothing is supposed to wait while atoms are still initializing, but `CreateAtoms` drops its mapload state whenever it sleeps, so `initializing_something()` was pretty much never true mid-load.

These runtimes most commonly happen when bitrunning safehouses load async inside the domain's own load, finish first, and release their smoothing while the domain is still asleep. Smoothing then reads the walls next door, which haven't initialized yet and still have their smoothing groups as a raw string. 

Fix is a counter of `InitializeAtoms` wrapped around `CreateAtoms`, which is what `initializing_something()` checks now. Same idea as the original counter from #75444.

Negligible performance impact compared to the more complicated solutions

## Why It's Good For The Game

Fixes a very ANNOYING and spammy runtime that I've seen for a long time.

changes.text: bitrunning safehouse walls and windows no longer try to connect to walls that don't fully exist yet

title: Fix atmos gas relocation during pipeline rebuilds
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

When any pipe in a network is destroyed, that network's pipeline is deleted and only rebuilt on `SSair`'s next fire. Until then, every machine attached to it still has its neighboring pipe (`nodes[i]`) but no pipeline (`parents[i]` is null). If the machine is destroyed in that window, which explosions do all the time, `relocate_airs()` takes the neighbor to mean there is a pipeline and runtimes:

```
Runtime in code/modules/atmospherics/machinery/components/components_base.dm,406: Cannot read null.air
  proc name: relocate airs (/obj/machinery/atmospherics/components/proc/relocate_airs)
```

No meaningful performance gain/loss detected in benchmarks (slight perf in some places, slight loss in others, in ns..The only thing that calls this is the destruction proc so it doesn't matter anyway.

Also found a probable oversight with TEG circulators? They just delete their gas if destroyed unlike other atmos machines

## Why It's Good For The Game

This is not hot code and the lack of runtimes makes it worth it.

changes.text: atmos machines destroyed in explosions now release the gas inside them instead of sometimes deleting it.

thermoelectric generator circulators (both hot and cold) no longer delete the gas inside them when destroyed or deconstructed. the gas now goes into the pipes they're connected to, or onto the floor if they aren't connected.

title: Adds two fertilizers
author: the-orange-cow
body:
## About The Pull Request

Adds two new fertilizers. Chemo Cultivate reduces weed rate and weed chance while also reducing plant endurance and lifespan. Stabili Feed reduces instability while having a per unit chance of deleting a random trait or reagent from the plant. The are available at both the biogenerator and the special lavaland seed vault chem dispencer.

Buffs the endurance gain of Enduro Grow.

Several insignificant punctuation changes.

## Why It's Good For The Game

FYI, I kind of guessed at the values for all of this. I'm more than willing to adjust them if need be.

Currently, weed rate and weed chance are functionally one way streets when it comes to botany stat manipulation. Although there are ways for a competent botanist to deal with them, it seems odd that the primary engine for plant stat adjustments does not. Chemo Cultivate adds in such a method, while still requiring care due to the damage it does to a plant's lifespan and endurance.

Although methods of increasing instability are readily available shiftstart in the form of L4Z, no fertilizer that you don't need a chem dispenser for decreases instability(Robust Harvest doesn't count, fight me). Reducing instability on a plant, that is, turning down the genetic heat, doesn't seem like it should be a particularly high hurdle. Stabili Feed reduces instability, although not to the extent more premium fertilizers may, as well as has a stacking chance of randomly removing traits and reagents from a plant as a balance.

The point of both of these changes it to fill what feels like holes in the plant stat manipulation system.

I also buffed the endurance gain on Enduro Grow. The main time I ever use it is when the chef asks for high quality food(food quality is based on endurance + lifespan in plants), and it takes a while, and overall seems insignificant otherwise. I threw this in on a whim, I don't mind removing it if the powers that be see fit.

changes.text: New fertilizer at your local biogenerator, Chemo Cultivate. Reduces weeds, reduces lifespan and endurance of plants. Use with care.
New fertilizer at your local biogenerator, Stabili Feed. Reduces instability, has a chance of culling plant traits and reagents. USE WITH EXTREME CARE.

title: Make `held_items` a protected var (fuck downstreamers!!!!!)
author: tontyGH
body:
## About The Pull Request

`held_items` is now only accessible to subtypes of `mob`. Anything that did not adhere to this was corrected.
These procs were added to make interfacing with held_items possible:
- `/mob/proc/get_hand_slots() as /list` returns a copy of `held_items`
- `/mob/proc/get_held_items() as /list` returns *currently held items*
- `/mob/proc/get_held_items_of_type() as /list` returns currently held items filtered by a given type
- `/mob/proc/get_held_items_of_typelist() as /list` returns currently held items filtered by a *list of types*
- `/mob/proc/get_active_held_indexes() as /list` returns the indexes of currently held items


Additionally, these procs were altered:

- `/mob/proc/is_holding` now returns a TRUE/FALSE boolean instead of the located instance.
- `/mob/proc/get_empty_held_indexes` is now no longer nullable and always returns a list
- `/mob/proc/can_hold_items` now returns a TRUE/FALSE boolean instead of the length of `held_items`.
- `/mob/proc/is_holding_item_of_types` no longer ignores the 2nd+ paths specified.

Downstreams will need to audit all uses of `held_items` and the above procs to properly merge this PR.

Due to the nature of this PR, a lot of code was reviewed and rewritten to be more efficient or logically consistent. 

## Why It's Good For The Game

Abstracting how hands work from users will allow us to more easily modify how hands work internally, which will be useful for my refactor later.

Sleeping Carp's style malus did not ignore "cool" held items

title: Fixes a few hard deletes that were causing flaky runtimes
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request
Three for one.

```
## REF SEARCH Found /obj/item/melee/baseball_bat [0x2059604] in /mob/living/carbon/human/consistent's [0x300149a] back var.
## REF SEARCH Found /obj/item/melee/baseball_bat [0x2059604] in /mob/living/carbon/human/consistent's [0x3001588] back var.
```

Monkeys spot a weapon on the floor and walk over to it. If someone picked it up in the meantime, the pickup still went ahead and pulled it out of their inventory. 

The monkey dropped it through its own unequip, which cleared the item's `IN_INVENTORY` flag and moved it without the real owner ever letting go. That owner's slot kept pointing at the item, and the item hard deleted once it got deleted:

The ground pickup now gives up if the item isn't lying on a turf anymore. Snatching from hands still goes through the victim's own unequip, unchanged.

**Mirrors holding onto deleted mobs.** The reflection component registered for deletion with `RegisterSignals(target, COMSIG_QDELETING, ...)`. That loops over a list, and a single signal string makes it register nothing, so the mirror never let go of something it tracked unless it saw it step off one of its turfs:

```
## REF SEARCH Found /mob/living/carbon/human/consistent [0x3001503] in list Datums -> /datum/component/reflection [0x2101e9ba] -> reflected_movables (list).
```

Same issue, this should be RegisterSignal.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Fewer flaky hard deletes in create and destroy, bugfixes

title: Centers bodypart texture filters
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request Follow-up to #97699. Bodypart textures (suit meshes, the voidwalker curse, and the infusion textures) didn't cover the whole of large sprites like wings. #97699 tiles a texture across large overlays with one filter per 32px tile, at offsets `0, 32, 64, 96`. But BYOND places a filter's icon centred on the image, not at its bottom-left corner. So on a 96px wide sprite the tiles end up only covering the middle third, the right third, while the left third is never textured. The same happens vertically. Wings are now also flagged `LIMB_OVERLAY_TALL_ICON`. `wings.dmi` is 96x34, and 23 frames (megamoth, mothra and others) have art in the top or bottom row. A single row of centred tiles misses those rows; before, the off-centre loop covered the top row by accident and never the bottom one. title: Followup update_sight refactor fixes
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

Follow-up to #97867, fixing three bugs it introduced.

`restore_initial_sight()` threw away the sight it built. It added the ventcrawl `SEE_TURFS|BLIND` and the return values of `COMSIG_LIVING_RESTORE_INITIAL_SIGHT` handlers to `init_sight`, then returned `initial(sight)`. 

So ventcrawlers saw mobs and objects normally from inside the pipes. It also reset `lighting_color_cutoffs` after sending that signal, which wiped the tint the cyborg meson and thermal handlers had just applied.

- It now resets the cutoffs first, then sends the signal, and returns `init_sight`.
- The ventcrawl sight also requires the mob to actually be inside a pipe. When a vent is destroyed with a mob inside, the mob is dumped out still holding `TRAIT_MOVE_VENTCRAWLING`, because only `handle_ventcrawl()` removes it. Without this check, that mob would stay blind until it ventcrawled again. Before #97867 this sight came from the pipe being `client.eye`, so it only ever applied inside one.

The cyborg thermal toggle couldn't turn off. `/datum/action/cooldown/borg_thermal/Activate()` passed the signal name `COMSIG_LIVING_RESTORE_INITIAL_SIGHT` to `HAS_TRAIT_FROM` as if it were a trait, so the check was never true. Every press took the "turn on" branch, and the second press threw an "overridden" stack trace from re-registering the signal. It now checks `TRAIT_THERMAL_VISION`, and the off branch unregisters the signal it actually registered.


Other things: 

Engineering goggles gave meson vision while off. `/obj/item/clothing/glasses/meson/engine` inherited `TRAIT_MESON_VISION` from plain mesons. Engineering scanner goggles had meson vision in their off mode until cycled.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Bugfixes

engineering and mining cyborgs' meson vision and syndicate saboteur cyborgs' thermal vision tint dark areas again.

engineering scanner goggles only give meson vision in meson mode again. Shuttle region scanners, atmospheric thermal imaging goggles and admin imaging goggles no longer give meson vision at all.

- `after_throw()` was clearing `IN_INVENTORY` right after `throw_impact()` put the item in the catcher's hand, so anything you caught was only sort of in your inventory. Dribbling a caught ball put it in both hand slots and the second drop had no wielder. That line's a leftover from the examine tooltips PR (#28407) back when the flag only did tooltips, unequipping already clears it so we can safely get rid of it.
- `put_in_hands()` calls `dropped()` without ever equipping the ball when the catcher's hands are full, so there might not be a wielder at all.
- Holding two balls and dropping the one with the signals left them on the dropped ball, so getting knocked down would fumble the ball that was already on the floor and drag it back to you.

Now only one ball in your hands has the signals, and if you drop it they move over to your other ball (new sentence unlocked...).

## Why It's Good For The Game

runtimes-b-gone, fix bug

a basketball you've let go of no longer keeps bouncing when you walk, or gets pulled back to your feet when you're knocked down

## About The Pull Request

- If you were inside something (vent, disposals, closet, mech) while your cuffed item lay outside, every move made the leash pathfind and teleport the item after you, and the chain got redrawn from the item to the bottom left corner of the map.[^1] Disposals did it every tick. - Fixed a runtime when the owner got deleted with the item on the floor. Added unit tests.

[^1]: On our downstream a monkey cuffed a briefcase of loot to itself and crawled through vents. Every step pushed time dilation up to 30%.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Less lag, no broken chain, and you can uncuff someone's item again.

title: Dragonsbreath shells: Printable, go FWOOSH and also bounce. Yay! (New change: incendiaries also go fwoosh)
author: necromanceranne
body:
## About The Pull Request

Dragonsbreath shells are no longer crafted, and instead are printable from the security lathe when researched with Riot Suppression tech. 

Rather than leave trails behind, ~~dragonsbreath~~ incendiary projectiles detonate in a small fire blast when it hits something or expires. This just sets everything in surrounding tiles on fire. But it also super sets the person on fire the person who was shot by multiple pellets if hit with dragonsbreath.

Rocket launcher fire trails and flamethrower trails do not cause the burst, and obviously still leave a trail. Junk flame rounds do burst because it'd be really funny.

Also, dragonsbreath bounces. Why? So you can flush out tight corridors with it, obviously.

~~Also gives it some familiar stats regarding damage falloff because as it turns out, this is just buckshot again in a fiery package.~~

Changes the damage values of incendiary projectiles to have an equivalent amount of force to their standard counterpart -5. This should be equal to the AP projectile in most cases. This has largely increased the base damage of incendiary projectiles across the board.

### Misc Changes

I changed the name of the tesla cannon design datum because it's not a stun revolver.

Also mades the AP 9mm deal 25 and not 27 damage. This was a bizarre outlier because almost every other AP projectile is -5. 

## Why It's Good For The Game

[My reasoning.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TysIkGtf_a8)

I hate the craftable shells. This one is the easier to get out of the crafting menu. 

I don't like the fire trails, I think it is more harmful than useful.

At the damage values they were dealing, incendiary projectiles were almost always a bad decision if you were trying to kill people, which you presumably are given you are setting them on fire. Setting someone on fire is not necessarily killing them any faster. You are actually killing them far slower. So it begs the question as to what exactly are these projectiles doing if not killing people in a blazing mess?

They kinda failed to do either of these things most of the time. Made worse by the proliferation of fire resistant suits/body level fire resistance. We still want the person getting shot to be _shot_.

It demonstrates just how callous a given security officer is when he's hitting you with dragonsbreath. Ops too.

changes.text: Dragonsbreath is now printable with Riot Suppression tech. They are no longer crafted.
Incendiary now conflagrates in a small fireball for each pellet that hits. They no longer leaves a fire trail.
Incendiary projectiles now do more damage on the projectile itself.
Dragonsbreath also now bounces.

title: Removes skeleton keys
author: necromanceranne
body:
## About The Pull Request

What it says on the tin. Tendril crates can simply be opened to obtain the loot within.

## Why It's Good For The Game (I'm Going To Rant)

We changed how tendrils work entirely to instead function as mini-bosses. This is enough friction to no longer need to worry about people focusing down tendrils to the exclusion of mining. This is also for the sake of consistency with other boss fauna.

Anyway, time for a rant because I went and re-read the PR that added keys, so I now need to vent:

[It didn't work.](https://github.com/tgstation/tgstation/pull/56267#issuecomment-765691326) People definitely still went and rushed tendrils after this change because it assumed that the people rushing those tendrils were not mining at all. They were. They absolutely were.

You need to actually mine towards the location of those tendrils in order to get their loot. And, typically, there is enough ore between wherever you started and wherever you intended to go to handily get a key for your chests without putting in terribly much effort at all. The same could be said of boss rushers, but people could almost certainly no-hit many of the bosses during that period with ease, so I'm not even sure they even had to resupply. And, granted, once those miners did kill the boss mobs, they usually just fucked off from lavaland for good, which is what really put a stop to ore recovery then and there.

This PR in retrospect feels like a whole bunch of folk misunderstanding the fundamental problem with mining (the actual mining part had very minimal incentives and the gameplay people are engaging in can be perfected such that they no longer need to engage in ore recovery at all to progress through that content regularly) and simply assumed that kicking the shins of its most approachable layman content was enough to put those miners in their place. Completely ignoring the fact that the solution they have come up with doesn't even remotely hinder the actual people engaging in that content OR the people who may have actually been the problem elements in the first place. Rather, it just kind of put a child safety cap on mining loot so assistants with a pickaxe can't just come down and steal a bunch of it for themselves. Which is nice I guess but not at all what the PR set out to accomplish. And I think the tendrils now eating you for being so presumptuous about getting their loot is a lot more interesting a disincentivization.

Anyway, mining is a whole lot more cohesive in the modern era, you do get generally equal rewards for engaging in all parts of the content and boss rushing is not nearly as desirable as it was previously to the exclusion of everything else due to the possibility of missing out on further progression that ISN'T boss loot, so this shit is a fucking relic and doing nothing anymore. Let's put it to rest.

title: [MDB Ignore] Remove holopay stand and vend-a-tray, add tip jars
author: MrMelbert
body: ## About The Pull Request Removes the holopay stand completely Removes the vend-a-tray completely In the place of the kitchen vend-a-trays, there are now simple tip jars, which you can put coins and cash into. You can also build tip jars with glass sheets (even plasmaglass sheets). ## Why It's Good For The Game - Why remove the holopay stand? The holopay stand is a neat little thing but it over-complicates an otherwise simple action. As a consequence it is barely used. For people setting up face-to-face shops, it's significantly easier to exchange money by hand instead of making people swipe their card on the scanner. For people setting up remote shops, there exists another method of remote pay - nt pay - that is easier for both parties to understand. And, personally, I think the holopay stand is just out of place for the setting. It follows the trend of "well if we stick `holo-` to something we don't need to explain how it works" that feels a little immersion breaking. Perhaps there could exist a version of it where it gets summoned from a holopad, but as it stands I think the pay app has better verisimilitude. - Why remove the vend-a-tray? The vend-a-tray is, again, a nifty little thing that calls back to diner food displays, but it has some issues on its own. For one, no one uses it[1][2]. I could count the amount of times I saw food in one of those things over the last year on one hand. For two, even if the chef uses it, the crew doesn't, for a number of reasons[3][4]. As a consequence, the vend-a-tray ends up being just a waste of counter space. [1] *Chefs generally don't like to require payment for food. Their job is to feed people and requiring payment means less people get fed which means you aren't doing your job.* [2] *You can only put one item on it. If you want to sell multiple food items, you either need to make more trays or you need to babysit it.* [3] *No one likes to pay for food or drink. People are perfectly willing to tip the chef or bartender, but when you start charging, people would rather just not eat, because the downsides to not eating aren't very severe.* [4] *There's not many food items worth paying for, outside of roleplay. Food buffs aren't particularly fleshed out for a number of reasons, so putting "good food" for a price doesn't mean much if you're also offering "decent food" for free. And to circle back to the 'outside of roleplay' point, if you are roleplaying, you could just as easily exchange money by hand instead of automating it.* - The bigger point I'm kind of against automated shop fronts and remote money transfer. Being an interaction driven roleplaying game, face-to-face exchange of money *should be* the primary way of bartering. Replacing it with automation removes potential interactions. You can't haggle or try to pickpocket or intimidate a paystand. I'm not a fan of remote pay for a similar reason, but I think having one method of wireless transfer for the sandbox is alright. And as for custom vendors, I'm also vaguely OK with it due to the overall importance of vendors to the economy (also you can tip them over or whatever and that's funny). That's why I went with adding a tip jar in the place of trays - Simpler than the holopay stand (with better verisimilitude), and more potential for interaction than a vend-a-tray.

changes.text: Removed the ability for id cards to project a pay stand
Removed the vend-a-tray entirely

You can construct tip jars with glass or plasmaglass (though not with their reinforced variants). Tip jars accept many tiny methods of gratuity, such as coins, cash, holochips, IOUs, or... a cigarette, sure.
Adds tip jars to the kitchen in the bar, where the vend-a-trays once sat.

title: NT Shopping Network no longer resends the whole cargo catalogue every second while it's open

title: Give Mothpeople 4 arms (Mothperson Rework)
author: tontyGH
body:
## About The Pull Request Mothpeople get 2 extra arms which are an innate part of their chest (replacing the chest removes the extra arms, implanting the chest gives you them). The hands are fully articulate, so they can do anything that your lower set of arms can do. It was a conscious decision to make the extra arms tied directly to the chest and not be a special organ, I foresaw people implanting these on much stronger chests (like human/cyborg) and nullifying the downside. This could change in the future, but right now I'm pretty confident. Notably, these extra arms aren't tied to any body zones, meaning you cannot directly interact with them in any way. Since you can't target them, you cannot damage, wound, dismember, operate on, augment or replace these arms. However, disabling the chest (via severe chest fracture) will also disable the limbs.
Balance concerns: ### Handcuffing? You only need one pair of handcuffs to fully cuff moths. Because of how handcuffing works, you will simply always be able to handcuff a mothperson, even if both their main arms are missing. This is not a concern. ### Stripping?
The strip menu was overhauled to accomodate the possibility of multiple hands.
You won't see the extra hands if the target doesn't have them, so there won't be any redundant info. ### Dual-wielding? Dual-wielding is handled correctly, and you will put the other item in your offhand. You can freely swap to your other free hands, but the offhand will be unavailable. Being able to dual-wield multiple weapons is not as strong as it initially seems because of click delay. Having two axes does not increase DPS in the same way that having two butchers knives won't work. ### Akimbo?
I mean, you can try. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd2f42e0-b9b3-47a7-aff2-5606fa2f8dc5
This is much easier to control intentionally with the Left/Right hand keybinds, since they let you cycle between sets. ## Why It's Good For The Game Could be interesting. Mothpeople are somewhat of a boring species right now since they're basically just humans with wings. I can't actually say with confidence how this will play out, so I'm putting few limitations on the upper arms so we can see what's strong and then work from there. I don't think it'd be great to make this immediately useless.

There's now a flag for when the startup distribution has actually happened (it's set before the rock edge pass, since that can sleep). title: Reworks misfing to be based on chamber pressure, .38/.357 are interchangable, junk rounds are shotgun shells again
author: necromanceranne
body:
## About The Pull Request

Completely reworks how misfiring rounds works. To accomplish this, we've removed alternative calibers entirely, since misfiring was only reason to retain these mechanics. ~~Except one instance where I'm kind of a bit suspicious about.~~

### Malfunctions

Guns and ammo now have chamber pressure mechanics. 

Ammunition is assigned a pressure value; Low, Medium or Extreme. This is in ascending order from left to right in power.

Guns have a pressure threshold: Low, Medium or Extreme.

If the pressure of the ammo exceeds the threshold of the gun, the gun begins to degrade in performance. 

Degradation leads to the possibility of malfunction: 

- Misfire (hurting you) if the ammo that is being fired is over pressure. 
- If the ammunition is at the expected pressure for the gun, it can instead fail to fire a round if it would roll a malfunction.

### .357 and .38 are interchangeable rounds

In real life, .38 is the same size as .357, so these rounds can usually be safely fired from guns chambered for the latter. This is not the same in the reverse, as guns rated for .38 Special are not necessarily able to handle the pressure of the full power .357.

We now simulate this interaction more intuitively than before. Previously, you had to wrench the gun to use the alternative caliber. Now, you just need to load it into any compatible gun.

This definitely will only go well.

To make this, like, moderately saner, there have been some balance changes;

- .38 revolvers now have a max misfire probability of 50%. Firing one .357 will hit this max. (Remember, you only roll for misfires on subsequent shots)
- .357 bullets now have a base damage of 40. However, .357 revolvers you can obtain in the game have a damage multiplier of x1.5, bringing it back up to 60 force. 
- .38 speedloaders and .357 speedloaders cannot fit the other kind of round.
- BR-38 magazines can fit .357. The BR-38 increases the damage to 48 because it has an inherent damage buff.
- However, firing .357 once from a BR-38 causes it to immediately start malfunctioning at max degradation. Good luck stringing multiple shots together.

### Junk Rounds are shotgun shells again

With the new pressure mechanics, we can let junk rounds be fired from shotguns again, and pipeguns fire shotgun shells again.

We do this by making junk rounds have extreme pressure. (We also applied this to old buckshot)

Riot shotguns, compact combat shotguns and double-barreled shotguns are rated for medium pressure.

Pipeguns, pipe pistols, combat shotguns and bulldog shotguns are rated for extreme pressure.

To keep pipeguns from experiencing the same damage nonsense as combat shotguns did when they got a damage buff, pipegun damage multiplier went down from x1.75 to x1.6. This doesn't really affect junk rounds too terribly much, but does mean you can't one-shot someone into stamina crit with rubber shot.

### Gun Integrity Loss from Ammo

This sucks so I took it out.

## Why It's Good For The Game

I've wanted to futz with these mechanics more for a bit, and I've wanted to marry .38 and .357 for a fairly long time. The way we handled this before just kind of blew chunks. Hopefully this is a bit more elegant and user friendly.

Pipeguns/pipe pistols fitting shotgun shells isn't that impactful for most shell types, as the majority don't do as much damage as a junk round already does. The exception is rubbershot because we overtuned it on purpose. People were kind of upset to lose junk rounds in shotguns, so...here they are again. Kinda. You might just misfire shotgun into yourself for using them though.

Integrity loss from shooting guns isn't super duper clear and I prefer the degradation mechanics instead.

changes.text: Misfiring has been completely reworked.
.38 and .357 are interchangeable in all compatible guns without needing to wrench the gun. Just load it in! Nothing bad could possibly happen.
Junk rounds are once again shotgun rounds, and pipeguns/pipe pistols now fit shotgun shells again.
Guns now have pressure mechanics to handle misfiring. Check you gun carefully to determine its pressure rating.

Old buckshot no longer breaks your gun. Literally. As in it no longer damages the gun directly and makes it vanish suddenly. Old buckshot will still fuck up your gun because someone loaded in too much powder.

title: Fix ghost poll follow link doing nothing
author: 13spacemen
body:
## About The Pull Request

The `(F)` follow link in the "X Poll: ckey was selected." announcement did nothing when clicked.

`announce_chosen()` runs before the poll returns, so the link was built from the chosen candidate's observer. The caller then moves the candidate's key into their new mob, and the old observer deletes itself in `/mob/dead/observer/Logout()`. By the time anyone clicks, `locate()` on the link returns null.

This PR points the link at the chosen client instead. The observer `follow` Topic handler now resolves a client to its current mob when the link is clicked, so the link follows the player into whatever body they were given.

title: Fix tgui prompts with sequential prompts bugging out if you click/enter too fast
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

When DM closes a tgui window and opens the next UI in the same pooled window, the suspend and the next update can both reach the page before React renders. 

This causes the next window to never open for the client.

Can easily be reproduced if you open a window that opens a second window of the same interface, like the Jump To Coordinate ui for example, Submit an option within ~67 ms of opening that closes the window.
Watch the next window never open, so it looks like it's being canceled out to the user. A frustrating experience if it happens later in the sequence, like on the last coord.

The fix is to render the suspended state synchronously in `suspend()` with `flushSync`, so the next update always mounts a fresh interface.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Fixes an annoying bug

title: Fix getting deafened during TTS permanently muting all game sounds
author: sohpeach
body:
## About The Pull Request

Fixes at least one cause of #95456. I didn't really see a cleaner way to ensure this field is set without messing with all the playesound functions.

TTS lines are played through `/datum/threed_sound`. It's passed a channel, but never applies the channel to the sound. The channel is eventually applied once `playsound_local` is called, which `play_tts` calls for each listener first, but it returns early for deaf mobs. Mobs that are already deaf when something is said aren't TTS listeners at all, but listeners can go deaf in between a message being sent and TTS being played (due to a bomb going off, for example). If everyone who heard the line is deaf by the time it plays, the sound keeps channel 0.

`threed_sound` resends the sound whenever the listener or the speaker moves. While the listener is deaf it is sent with `SOUND_MUTE|SOUND_UPDATE`, and on channel 0 that mutes every sound on the client. If the TTS line ends before the listener can hear again, the unmute is never sent, and the game stays silent until the window is closed and reopened. As the issue says, reconnecting doesn't help.

`threed_sound` now sets its channel on the sound when it's created.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Being deaf bad.

## Testing

Setup:
- I don't have a TTS server, so I ran a small stand-in on localhost and pointed `TTS_HTTP_URL` at it. It returns one voice from `/tts-voices`, and answers every `/tts*` request with an ogg after a 1.5 second delay, with `audio-length: 4`.
- DreamSeeker controlled a human in a hallway. An NPC human with a TTS voice stood on the next tile. My admin ghost was moved to another z-level, so the client's mob was the only one who heard the line.
- I recorded only DreamSeeker's audio with OBS and measured when each sound started.

It's hard to distribute this testing setup.

Each run was scripted using Lua:
1. Four beeps (`playsound_local`) to the client's mob (one per second).
2. The NPC says a line.
3. Half a second later, the client's mob takes ear damage (`adjust_temporary_deafness(8 SECONDS)`), before the TTS audio has come back.
4. The line plays while the mob is deaf. The NPC steps back and forth every half second for 10 seconds, which covers the whole line.
5. The 4 second line ends, then the mob's hearing comes back on its own a few seconds later.
6. Eight more beeps, then one on the admin channel (1023) and one on a fixed channel (900).

The server logs confirmed that events happened in this order.

Results:
- On master, none of the beeps after hearing returned were heard, in 3 out of 3 runs, and the client stayed silent until DreamSeeker was restarted. In a control run with the NPC standing still, all of them were heard.
- With this change, all of them were heard in 3 out of 3 runs.

changes.text: Being deafened while a TTS line is about to play no longer mutes all game sounds until you reopen the game.

title: Fix charges and transit tubes going instant late in a round
author: sohpeach
body:
## About The Pull Request

I thought this might fix #97900, but if that issue starts after 1 hour rather than 2.67 hours I don't really see how this could be the problem.

SSmovement files move loops into buckets keyed by `"[time]"`. Turning a number into text keeps 6 significant digits, so once `world.time` reaches 100000 (2 hours 47 minutes after the world started, lobby and init included) different times start sharing a key: `100001.5`, `100002` and `100002.5` all become `"100002"`.

When a loop is processed and requeued for its next step, its new time can then map to the bucket that is still being processed. It gets added to that bucket's list and runs again in the same tick, and again, until its timeout runs out. That happens to loops with a delay of 0.5 or 1 deciseconds, so mob charges (0.5) cover their whole distance in one tick and transit tube pods (1 per straight tube) cross a whole line of tubes in one tick. Other loops can land in a bucket for a slightly earlier time and step up to a decisecond early.

The keys now use `num2text(time, 12)`, which keeps every digit a move loop time can have. `queue_loop()` and `smash_bucket()` also build the key once instead of two or three times.

Added a unit test that queues loops for 100001.5, 100002 and 100002.5 and checks they end up in separate buckets. It fails on master and passes with this change.

The burning lantern is currently a bit boring: its sprite is a generic lantern with a bland green palette, and its passive effect isn’t terribly exciting.

title: Fixes parrying someone else's projectile using the boost multipliers
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

`attempt_parry()` sets the projectile's firer to the parrier and then checks `source.firer == user` to pick the multipliers, so it _always_ picked the boost ones. Don't think that was the intent.

Now, parrying someone else's projectile uses `parry_speed_mult` and `parry_damage_mult` like it was meant to, and boosting your own shot still uses the boost ones.

This does mean parried shots (watcher beams, colossus bolts, herald shots, etc) now get 1.15x damage and 1.25x speed instead of 1.5x and 1.6x, which is what the component's defaults say they should be.

## Why It's Good For The Game

title: Fixes new tgui windows closing themselves while they load on people with slow PCs or connections
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

`process()` closes any UI that hasn't initialized within `TGUI_PING_TIMEOUT` (4 seconds) of `open()`. That makes sense for a pooled window answering a ping, but a window that has to create its browser also has to load the whole bundle first, and that counts against the same 4 seconds. On a slow first load you get `Zombie window detected, closing.` on a window that was just about to work.

Sets a more generous deadline once in `open()`: **60 seconds** when the window still has to start its browser, the usual `TGUI_PING_TIMEOUT` when it's a pooled window getting a ping. `process()` only compares against it, so it's one subtraction less than before, no performance difference.

Held a new window's page load for 6 seconds:
- before: closed as a zombie 4.15s after initialize
- after: stays open, ready at 6.7s

Benched `process()` the same way, 30 paired runs of 10k sweeps, difference is within noise:
- 1 UI: 13.87ms -> 13.82ms
- 9 UIs: 111.34ms -> 111.02ms

## Why It's Good For The Game

UIs closing on people with slow PCs or connections

changes.text: tgui windows that take more than 4 seconds to load the first time no longer close themselves

title: Fix ceruleans bricking shoes they pick up (+ small rendering cleanup)
author: MrMelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

```dm
/obj/item/clothing/shoes/proc/oh_what_a_neat_hat(mob/living/carbon/user, up_or_down)
	if(user && !(user?.bodyshape & BODYSHAPE_CERULEAN))
		return
	if(up_or_down)
		slot_flags |= ITEM_SLOT_HEAD
		detach_clothing_traits(clothing_traits)
	else
		slot_flags = initial(slot_flags)
		worn_y_offset = initial(worn_y_offset)
```
This proc removes clothing traits, and never re-adds them.
So any time a cerulean picked up a pair of shoes with clothing traits, the shoes would be permanently bricked.

I fixed this by refactoring the shoe logic a bit: `give_clothing_traits` now exists for clothing items. Shoes now check that the wearer is not a cerulean before giving clothing traits.

However in testing I broke shoe rendering somehow. Or maybe it was already broken. Regardless, I fixed it by changing a tiny bit of item rendering.

`build_worn_icons` `isinhands` now passes held index, rather than `TRUE`. `get_worn_offsets` uses this to determine offsets.

title: Energy Projectiles: Pulse/Shotgun Pulse, X-Ray and Smoothbore Disabler
author: necromanceranne
body:
## About The Pull Request

Pulse beams and x-ray laser beams are now subtypes of lasers, not beams.

Pulse projectiles have 50 AP (they're clearly anti-materiel) and have an increased flight speed. 

Shotgun pulse slugs have 40 damage instead of 30, and AP of 30, so less than the rifle version, but close enough. The intention here is to treat them like they have a standard equivalent; in this case, scatter laser is considered the equivalent, so we take the damage of scatter laser and reduce by -5 to then give them some kind of bonus effect. Which is AP.

On the topic of AP lasers, x-ray has had a damage bump because it is also functionally existing in this same space, but at 15 damage it is not quite doing enough to be meaningfully impactful unless shooting into extreme amounts of armor. We've pushed that up to 20 so it is sitting in that -5 sweet spot.

Smoothbore disablers no longer have an inaccuracy penalty, and have a damage bonus of x1.5 and speed bonus of x2. That puts them at 45 damage a shot. As they're weak to armor and need to be recharged each shot, it seems a bit unnecessary to also make them RNG shoot a wall. And I think it needs more oomph behind them to justify their usage while functionally being disablers only usable against soft targets. They also fly twice as fast too. Their prime version has a damage multiplier of x2.

## Why It's Good For The Game

These are some weapons that have felt a bit strange to me with time and could stand to get a revisit. 

Pulse slugs aren't very desirable because of various negatives they bring (they punch holes in the walls, which is toted as a positive, but for crew largely a negative unless exploited to get into a defensive position), they don't do much more damage than comparable alternative projectiles (They were outperformed by fucking rubbershot a lot of the time), and their construction makes them a bit annoying to make. 

Actual pulse is fine, but mostly is as potent as it is less for the projectile and more for the spammability of the projectile from the gun housing it, and the fact it removes cover very rapidly. I think them being actually horrifying to fight as anyone sells it a bit more that Nanotrasen isn't fucking around if you're being shot by this. You get a taste of it with the slugs with their lowered stats.

X-ray lasers just needed a bit more damage. [As explained here ](https://github.com/tgstation/tgstation/pull/97933), AP rounds generally have -5 the standard damage and that seems to be a sweetspot that makes them more useful to use even against soft targets, even if not ideal. Unless you were wallbanging someone, x-ray was flat not a good idea against all but the most heavily armored targets. At 20 force, there is a reason to still use it against even soft targets.

Smoothbores feel a bit weird next to the musket, its sister weapon. Both of them are for soft targets, but I think the last buff that muskets got put them head and shoulders above the smoothbore, even as a disabling weapon. I do really like the suggestion that their best use is fire and drop to pull out another smoothbore, but I think it is hampered by their low damage comparative to their vulnerability to armor, as well as their inaccuracy penalty that forces them to be used point blank or threaten to miss. 

Comparable weapons, the aforementioned musket and pipe pistol, at least bring either consistent damage for cheap reloads that encouraged a hit and run approach, or loads of upfront damage but a much lengthier reload process, making it better for assassinations or unloading a whole lot of pain into someone as an opener. Smoothbores just struggled to carve out any presence here. So there wasn't much reason to have one on you compared to alternatives. 

At 45 damage after multiplication, the gun now actually can slow a soft humanoid target enough to give distance if necessary. Great for how cheap it is, and also leaves no lasting harm so also good for nonlethal takedowns. Has a reason to be paired with other weapons to finish off a target, such as a stun prod.

changes.text: Pulse projectiles now have high armor penetration. They also move extremely quickly.
Pulse slugs do 40 damage and have an AP of 30.
X-ray lasers now do 20 damage instead of 15.
Smoothbore disablers no longer are inaccurate, and do 45 damage and move twice as fast. They still struggle to harm anything with armor.
